This practice has spread across various grades, enhancing students' sense of belonging and value. While affirmations alone do not replace effective teaching methods, they contribute to a supportive classroom atmosphere. Parents can also foster encouragement in their children by acknowledging their feelings and individuality.

articles.title: A mother who had to quit her Rs 50 LPA job, now changing chess scene in North India
articles.summary: After leaving her Rs 50 LPA corporate career to support her daughter Shivika’s chess ambitions, Nidhi Bhasin Rohilla discovered gaps in Delhi’s chess ecosystem. She set out to build what was missing, creating an academy, tournaments, and communities for players across ages and abilities. Today, her initiatives span eight states, championing accessibility, inclusion and a culture where chess thrives beyond ratings, titles and competition.

Nonprofit Touching Miami with Love plans to transform unused land behind its existing community centre into a five-storey development with 100 affordable homes. The project is expected to break ground in 2027, offering relief to families struggling with rising rents.

articles.title: From witchcraft to torture devices: 9 unusual museums around the world
articles.summary: Museums around the world reveal dark and unsettling narratives, immersing visitors in the macabre aspects of history and culture. The Vienna Crime Museum delves into the legacies of infamous criminals, while Amsterdam's Torture Museum displays chilling tools of punishment from Europe’s past. In Japan, the Meguro Parasitological Museum sheds light on the eerie world of parasites.

Yuvraj feels that not regularly considering these players for the ODI team does not do justice to their talent. He also hopes they get a place in the squad soon.

articles.title: Activist Arun Ferreira's arrest illegal, give him Rs 2 lakh: Bombay HC
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court has mandated that the Maharashtra government compensate activist Arun Ferreira with Rs 2 lakh. This ruling was based on the violation of Ferreira's fundamental rights under Articles 21 and 22, as he was arrested without valid identification and was not informed of the reasons for his detention.

articles.title: Total construction ban in Delhi-NCR from Nov 5 to 20
articles.summary: The national capital region will implement a complete ban on construction and demolition activities from November 5 to 20. This measure is part of a broader initiative to combat rising winter pollution levels. Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav confirmed that there would be no rollback of existing vehicle entry restrictions. Additionally, swift actions will target non-conforming industries and pollution hotspots in the region.

articles.title: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce donate $1 million to feed 2.4 million New Yorkers

Their $1 million contribution to New York's City Harvest is expected to help provide food to more than 2.4 million residents this summer. Several nonprofit leaders expressed shock and gratitude after learning about the unexpected gifts, which arrived as many communities face growing financial and food insecurity.

articles.title: ‘I did everything I could for India’: Poonam Raut on retirement and unfinished dream
articles.summary: After four years of chasing an India comeback, Poonam Raut has called time on her international career. In an exclusive conversation with TimesofIndia.com, the former India batter reflects on her retirement, the sacrifices her parents made to support her cricketing dream, her 86-run knock in the 2017 Women's World Cup final and the messages from young girls inspired by India's campaign. She also discusses women's cricket's growth and her plans to mentor young cricketers.

articles.title: 4 killed, 2 injured in fire at Delhi shoe factory; owner summoned
articles.summary: A fire broke out at a shoe manufacturing factory in Delhi's Mangolpuri Industrial Area, which killed four individuals. Firefighters responded quickly and managed to rescue six people trapped inside the building. Two injured victims were taken to Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Hospital for treatment following the incident. The cause of the fire is currently under investigation by local authorities and police personnel.

articles.title: 'The Time Is Now': How Phillips turned a John Cena moment into India's nightmare

Tanker with 27 Indian seafarers targeted in first-ever limpet mine attack in Hormuz
articles.summary: On October 29 and 30, two oil tankers were targeted in separate attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. MT LOUISE 1 was struck by limpet mines that caused a fire in its engine room. The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important oil export routes, connecting the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea. It has faced repeated security incidents since the conflict between US and Iran began.

articles.title: Elon Musk shares 'whole schedule' on how he spends time with his 14 children
articles.summary: Elon Musk recently disclosed details regarding his co-parenting schedule for his 14 children. He clarified that his five older children are adults living independently. Musk sees his kids with Claire every other week and his children with Shivon every few days. Contrary to claims, Musk stated that his arrangement is not corporate-like but personal. His children are grouped by their mothers, suggesting limited interaction between half-siblings.

Families are grappling with heightened expenses on essentials like food and fuel, resulting in diminished disposable incomes. This widening gap between income growth and the cost of living places a strain on households, particularly those with fixed financial obligations.

articles.title: Paid to hire, paid to work: Inside India’s Rs 99,446 cr plan to reshape formal workforce
articles.summary: Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) is introduced to enhance formal employment across various sectors. The scheme includes financial incentives for both employers and first-time employees entering the formal job market. PMVBRY aims to create more than 3.5 crore jobs including 1.92 crore first-time workers by 2027. It targets an increase in manufacturing employment with unique incentives for the sector.

articles.title: Kate Winslet reads 'Room on the Broom' for Storyline Online library
articles.summary: In a delightful initiative by Storyline Online, Kate Winslet recently narrated 'Room on the Broom,' a whimsical story that encourages literacy among children. Featuring a witch and her feline companion, the tale emphasizes themes of generosity and camaraderie, perfect for the Halloween spirit. Winslet's animated narration captivates young audiences, making reading a joy. With various celebrities contributing, Storyline Online provides a treasure trove of literature for families and schools alike.

articles.title: Melinda French Gates says her 2-day rule helps employees know they did a good job

This approach allows employees to feel secure in their performance evaluations as surprises are avoided. She emphasizes the importance of giving honest feedback with integrity while maintaining respect. Recently, Gates pledged $215 million to improve women's health and called for better accountability in healthcare systems.

articles.title: Woman uses inheritance to protect 140-acre Canadian island forest
articles.summary: Domena Diesing took a significant step by investing her grandmother's legacy to safeguard 140 acres of Lasqueti Island, Canada. By teaming up with the BC Parks Foundation, she secured a permanent conservation status for the land, enhancing a vast connected reserve now exceeding 1,000 acres in the Salish Sea. This project commemorates Alfred Gaensbauer’s enduring dedication to environmental preservation, ensuring a legacy of rich coastal habitats for generations to come.

The advice comes as AI-driven layoffs hit entry-level tech jobs the hardest.

articles.title: China may deploy orbital lasers to blind US satellites by late 2020s: Report
articles.summary: China's advancements in space-based directed-energy weapons are raising alarms, with operational capabilities potentially emerging by the late 2020s. These weapons threaten the integrity of enemy satellites, essential for contemporary military strategies. The US Defense Intelligence Agency has indicated that these developments expose significant vulnerabilities in US military satellite operations, jeopardizing crucial communication, navigation, intelligence, and missile warning systems, which are key to effective military engagement.

articles.title: Richard Simmons' Hollywood Hills home sells for $3.8m after $6.99m listing
articles.summary: After a price cut from $6.99 million, Richard Simmons' Sunset Strip estate has sold for $3.827 million. Initially listed in June 2025, the Colonial-style house piqued interest but failed to secure deals until now. The new buyer aims to preserve the home’s historical charm and scenic vistas while contemplating redevelopment in this sought-after area.

articles.title: Tea shop worker turned lawyer helps 30 tribal families, one lands govt job
articles.summary: Advocate V Akathiyan made a significant visit to Vayaloor village to aid 30 tribal families in acquiring overdue caste certificates, essential for expanding educational and job prospects. One of the beneficiaries, M Manikandan, secured a government clerk role thanks to the certificate. Akathiyan’s dedication also encompasses more tribal regions, addressing legal issues and fundamental necessities, showcasing how essential documentation can drive social equity.

articles.title: Bihar woman loses son to electric shock, starts solar irrigation for 38 farmers
articles.summary: Ladli Khatoon from Bahwanpur, Bihar, has transformed her family's tragedy into a solar irrigation venture. After losing her son, she discovered the risks of conventional irrigation methods and sought alternatives. Through support from JEEViKA and local organizations, she established a solar irrigation business, benefiting many farmers. This initiative has enabled several women to earn incomes and gain respect in their communities.

articles.title: 24 wins, 7 titles, 1 heartbreaking defeat: Wrestler Kalkal's winning streak ends
articles.summary: Sujeet Kalkal’s wait for a World Championships medal continued as the Indian wrestler suffered a heartbreaking defeat in the men’s 65kg quarterfinals on Thursday. Sujeet lost 3-3 on criteria to Tajikistan’s Abdulmazhid Kudiev, bringing his 24-match winning streak to an end.

California couple wins garden rights after neighbour’s 1955 deal for $250
articles.summary: A California couple who bought a home in 2019 found themselves in a legal battle after their neighbour claimed ownership of a 20-by-20-foot garden they believed was theirs. The dispute centred on a 1955 agreement involving $250, babysitting services and land access rights. On Monday, a California appeals court upheld the couple's exclusive right to use the garden.

articles.title: Insurance firm denied Rs 5 lakh to sister after brother's death, Allahabad HC overrules
articles.summary: The Allahabad high court has made a significant decision by siding with an unmarried sister in an insurance claim case, ordering Oriental Insurance Company to pay her Rs 5 lakh after her brother's death. Initially denied coverage due to her not being designated as a family member, the court made it clear that beneficiaries with documentation are entitled to benefits no matter the familial definitions.

articles.title: Big shake-up! MI confirm exits of three coaches, including Malinga
articles.summary: Mumbai Indians have parted ways with coaches Lasith Malinga, Paras Mhambrey and Carl Hopkinson ahead of IPL 2027. Malinga contributed to four IPL titles, while Mhambrey helped develop the team’s bowling talent and Hopkinson worked on fielding standards. The exits follow Mahela Jayawardene’s departure after mixed results in his second stint as head coach.

articles.title: Spain train crash: Audio reveals chilling exchange before deadly collision
articles.summary: According to the recordings published by Spanish outlets including El País and RTVE, a technical problem had disrupted the automatic signalling system, forcing trains on the affected stretch to stop. The system helps control train movements and prevents trains from entering sections of track when it may be unsafe to do so.

articles.title: Wife leaves at 5.17am, lover enters 3mins later: CCTV captures plot to kill husband
articles.summary: On October 26, a woman named Priya allegedly conspired with her gym trainer lover to stab her husband. CCTVs captured Priya leaving their home in Ghaziabad shortly before the attack occurred. The attack was brutal, happening while Shashank was asleep next to their young daughter. Shashank was immediately rushed to the intensive care unit after suffering severe injuries. Both Priya and her accomplice have been arrested and face multiple charges.

Younis emphasized Bumrah’s pivotal moments, especially during the T20 World Cup against Pakistan, while anticipating his return for the upcoming Test series against New Zealand next month.

articles.title: Brahmaputra-Kaveri link: India’s river-interlinking dream explained and the roadblocks ahead
articles.summary: India is working on an initiative to interlink rivers, particularly focusing on the connection between Brahmaputra and Kaveri. This proposal aims to address water scarcity in southern states, which often experience erratic rainfall. Several challenges exist, including interstate disputes, environmental concerns, and the need for technical feasibility. The Godavari-Kaveri link is critical in this proposal, but agreement among states remains complex.

articles.title: XUV700 booked in 2022, never delivered: Mahindra ordered to refund and pay Rs 62k

The manufacturer and dealer provided contradictory claims regarding the situation surrounding the delayed delivery. Consequently, the consumer commission found both parties guilty of unfair trade practices and ordered compensation.

The Monday decision confirms the trust's direct access to the lake and leaves an earlier $148,500 trespass award to neighbouring property owners cancelled. The dispute centred on conflicting land surveys dating back to 1997.

articles.title: 6 dead in MP: 2 sisters, one 8 months pregnant, and 4 children found in separate wells
articles.summary: Two sisters from Madhya Pradesh committed suicide by jumping into wells with their children on Wednesday. Anjali Rawat, who was eight months pregnant, took her son Prashant with her while Sita Rawat jumped with her three children. Family members reported the incidents after not seeing them return home. Each sister was profoundly impacted by personal tragedies occurring shortly before these events.

articles.title: TVK leader Christopher arrested for 'sexually harassing' college student

articles.title: Common anti-inflammatory drugs may help flu, COVID viruses spread: study
articles.summary: Researchers at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology have found that JAK inhibitors may weaken the body's defenses. These drugs can increase vulnerability to viral infections, such as COVID-19 and influenza. By suppressing immune responses, these medications facilitate easier spread of viruses within the body. Caution is advised for healthcare professionals when prescribing these drugs during outbreaks.

articles.title: 69-year-old writes 5,000+ free petitions since 1995, spends Rs 300 daily
articles.summary: Kannan N Ramakrishnan, who has been assisting people with grievances for nearly three decades, remains dedicated to public service. He transforms individuals' concerns into written petitions to present to government officials. Throughout his efforts, he has submitted over 5,000 petitions and covered a range of issues from civic problems to welfare benefits. Despite some petitions not yielding results, he finds satisfaction in helping others express their concerns.

articles.title: 3 siblings found dead in flat near Mumbai; trio recorded video before tragedy
articles.summary: Three siblings were discovered dead in their Virar flat, believed to have died by suicide. They recorded a video mentioning their health issues and financial troubles prior to their deaths. Residents noticed a foul smell and alerted the police, leading to the discovery of the bodies. One sibling suffered paralysis while another was undergoing cancer treatment, compounding their difficulties.

articles.title: Why Nike stayed away from the IPL for 18 years, and what brings it back
articles.summary: Nike has entered into a multi-year partnership with Mumbai Indians to supply kits from 2027. This partnership marks Nike's return to the IPL after almost two decades. The new gear will be presented to MI's teams ahead of their upcoming seasons. This move signifies Nike’s renewed commitment to the cricket market in India and reflects the growing demand for quality sports merchandise.

articles.title: Deaf children exposed to sign language from birth match hearing peers in early maths
articles.summary: A new study indicates that early access to language is crucial for children's understanding of numbers. Deaf children with exposure to sign language from birth perform similarly to hearing children learning spoken language. Researchers assessed various children, highlighting the importance of language in early development. The findings suggest that both signed and spoken languages foster academic skills, including mathematics.

articles.title: Paralysed at 18, Esme Gummer, 35, ran 5,000 km in 99 days
articles.summary: Esmée Gummer was left paralysed from the waist down after a surgery at the age of 18. She gradually learned to walk again, which later led her to discover a passion for running. Gummer completed a 5,000-km journey across the UK and Ireland, running for 99 consecutive days. As part of her initiative, she organized 76 inclusive running clubs that welcomed nearly 6,700 participants.

articles.title: Forces fortify key Arunachal bridge to fight dam objectors

The Central Armed Police Forces have been deployed to ensure order in the affected districts. Recent confrontations during a bandh left several people injured, including four women, escalating tensions. As supporters clashed with security, the Dite-Dime bridge emerges as a focal point of strife near the India-China border.

articles.title: 'Jailer 2' BO Day 15: Rajinikanth and Nelson’s film nears Rs 500 crore India gross

Candidates involved in violent activities aiming for regime change could be denied government jobs. However, political ideology alone cannot disqualify individuals from employment. The mere registration of an FIR or ongoing investigations will not automatically make candidates ineligible. Decisions on eligibility will depend on specific circumstances related to the verification rules.

articles.title: 'Better late than never': Why did F1 leave India, and why is it back on the agenda?
articles.summary: Tax disputes ended the Indian Grand Prix after three races. Thirteen years later, the government has put Formula 1 back on its agenda, with a task force examining the challenges that led to the sport’s exit, including taxation, import duties and commercial arrangements. As India targets a possible 2028 return, the big question is whether it can put the right framework in place for F1 to return - and stay.

Over 10 lakh vehicles in Gurgaon, Faridabad, Noida, Greater Noida, and Ghaziabad may be affected. Gurgaon and Faridabad hold around 2 lakh vehicles below BS6 standards, mostly consisting of BS3 and BS4 categories. Additionally, approximately 50,000 commercial vehicles in both locations do not comply with the new regulations.

articles.title: Two new Vande Bharat Sleeper trains to launch soon: Routes, timings, fares and more
articles.summary: Indian Railways is gearing up to introduce two innovative Vande Bharat Sleeper services, enhancing connectivity between major urban centers. The new Mumbai-Bengaluru route promises to shorten travel times, making it ideal for commuters and tourists. Additionally, the Varanasi-New Delhi service aims to improve overnight access for business travelers. With a focus on luxury and comfort, these services will elevate the passenger experience. Detailed schedules and pricing will be available shortly.

articles.title: IPL 2027: Gareth Batty likely to join CSK's support staff | EXCLUSIVE
articles.summary: Batty, who has played nine Tests, 10 ODIs and one T20I for England, is currently the head coach of Surrey in the County Championship.

articles.title: Can the man Trump called a 'jihadist' become America's first Muslim senator?
articles.summary: Donald Trump has called Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed a "jihadist" and accused him of extremist links without evidence. As El-Sayed faces Republican Mike Rogers in a closely contested race, can he overcome the controversy to become America's first Muslim senator?

articles.title: Mark Cuban says that he is not a doomer on AI, but believes in Cockroach Theory
articles.summary: Mark Cuban discussed the burgeoning role of artificial intelligence in reinforcing defenses against cyber threats, likening harmful AI entities to pesky cockroaches in his 'Cockroach Theory' of cybersecurity. He also showcased the Cost Plus Drug Company, which seeks to revolutionize pharmaceutical pricing through innovative 'pods' that facilitate medication manufacturing. This groundbreaking approach promises to significantly improve both healthcare accessibility and affordability in the near future.

articles.title: Jio Platforms IPO allotment: How to check, subscription details and listing date
articles.summary: Jio Platforms' initial public offering made waves with an unprecedented subscription rate, with allotment results to be finalized on Monday. The IPO opened from October 21 to October 23, garnering an impressive 22.19 times overall subscription. Approximately 1.3 crore applicants participated, leading to a staggering demand of Rs 7.5 lakh crore. Institutional investors were particularly active, subscribing at an astounding 70.55 times, while retail investors subscribed 2.72 times.

articles.title: Lawmaker seeks nearly 200 withheld texts in fight over Trump's Kennedy Center
articles.summary: A Democratic US lawmaker has asked a federal judge to order the Trump administration to release nearly 200 withheld text messages concerning Washington's Kennedy Center. The request comes amid a legal dispute over plans to close the performing arts centre for renovations, months after a judge ruled that Trump's name had been illegally added to the building and ordered its removal.

articles.title: Pakistan's Ayub released from squad in the middle of series, PCB explains why
articles.summary: Pakistan batter Saim Ayub has left the ODI tri-series squad to work on his batting after scoring three consecutive single-digit totals. Sahibzada Farhan has replaced him for the remaining matches. Pakistan have qualified for the final with three straight wins. Shadab Khan starred against England, scoring an unbeaten 113 to guide Pakistan to a thrilling one-wicket victory.

articles.title: How Myanmar dodged US sanctions to get Iranian jet fuel
articles.summary: Myanmar has reportedly masked Iranian jet fuel shipments as South African diesel in a bid to bypass US sanctions. An investigative reveal shows contracts that mislabel the cargo’s origin and characteristics. Such deceptive tactics complicate the enforcement of US sanctions against Iran. Previous shipments have also been traced back to Iran, heightening concerns. US officials are rigorously examining these developments amidst ongoing diplomatic dialogue with Myanmar.

articles.title: 'We hear you': Rahul's message to traders in Delhi amid anti-CEC stir
articles.summary: Rahul Gandhi has publicly backed the traders in Delhi struggling from the ramifications of ongoing protests and governmental restrictions. He pointed fingers at the administration for hampering commerce by suspending metro services and blocking roads. Traders are reportedly facing losses of around Rs 3,000 crore following previous rallies in October.

articles.title: Alaska Supreme Court upholds ban on 27-acre gravel mine over noise concerns
articles.summary: A gravel mine proposal by Beachcomber LLC in Anchor Point faced strong opposition from local residents. The Kenai Peninsula Borough Planning Commission initially rejected the permit due to significant environmental impact concerns. After several appeals and court rulings, the Alaska Supreme Court upheld the commission's decision in October 2026. The court found substantial evidence showed potential noise and visual disturbances could not be minimized.

articles.title: Cindy Crawford sold Malibu estate for $45m; Kim Kardashian paid $70.4m in 2022
articles.summary: In 2022, Kim Kardashian bought a Malibu mansion previously owned by supermodel Cindy Crawford. The property, originally listed at $99.5 million, sold for $70.4 million after several price reductions. This 3.18-acre estate features ocean views, a large swimming pool, and a private beach path. Initially acquired by Crawford and her husband in 2015, the home underwent significant renovations before the sale.

articles.title: United Airlines CEO wants the tax that made billionaires flee California across America
articles.summary: Scott Kirby, CEO of United Airlines, has voiced his support for a national wealth tax to address income inequality. He argues that implementing it nationally would mitigate wealthy individuals relocating to avoid taxes. Kirby also proposed increasing inheritance taxes to ensure fairness in the tax system. In a recent interview, he suggested requiring national service for all Americans to promote civic responsibility.

articles.title: Meet Sophia Fan, 17: Books under stairs inspired nonprofit sharing 7,000+
articles.summary: Sophia Fan initiated Literacy Cycle at the age of 13, aiming to provide educational resources to children. The nonprofit has reached over 7,000 books distributed across multiple states and a chapter in Rwanda. Originally focusing on AP textbooks, it now accepts various types of learning materials. Fan plans to continue this initiative while studying public or global health in college.

articles.title: Woman wins Rs 1.3L from travel agency after promised five-star stays were not provided
articles.summary: The consumer commission in Punjab has ruled in favor of Niti Bansal, instructing Club Infication to refund her Rs 1.2 lakh. Bansal, who purchased a luxury hotel membership meant for five years of five-star accommodations, encountered issues when she couldn't secure a reservation at Radisson. The commission identified serious service deficiencies and mandated the company to issue the refund and additional compensation within 60 days.

articles.title: Delhi’s 5km 'Namo Yamuna River Safari' to offer 40-minute rides at Rs 500
articles.summary: Delhi's chief minister Rekha Gupta inspected the Namo Yamuna River Safari project ahead of its upcoming launch. The soft launch is planned before the Chhath festival to allow families a new recreational option. Ticket prices for the 40-minute rides are set at Rs 500 per person, accommodating up to 30 passengers. The river safari aims to promote a clean and enjoyable experience on the Yamuna River.

articles.title: Zendaya buys house next door for over $2m, expands LA estate to half an acre
articles.summary: Zendaya began her real estate journey with a Mediterranean-style home purchased at age 20 in San Fernando Valley. She later acquired a ranch-style estate in Encino and a luxury condo in Brooklyn Heights. Recently, Zendaya bought a mid-century modern home in Hollywood Hills, previously owned by Ashley Tisdale. She subsequently purchased a neighboring property, a fixer-upper, signaling her intent to renovate it.

articles.title: Bihar DM joins schoolgirls for basketball during high school inspection
articles.summary: Tshering Y. Bhutia visited a government school in Kazisarai, Bihar, where she played basketball with students. Her engagement highlighted the importance of sports and regular physical activity in children's education. During another visit, she shared a midday meal with students to assess food quality and attendance. Bhutia's inspections focused on infrastructure and student concerns raised through the Vidyarthi Sahayog Portal.

articles.title: Why some people replay work conversations for hours, according to psychology
articles.summary: Rumination has a profound impact on individuals, fostering a cycle of repetitive thoughts about unsettling experiences and their consequences. This mental pattern often amplifies negative emotions while obstructing constructive problem-solving. Individuals may dwell on past discomfort and misinterpret these moments' importance. To break free from this cycle, distinguishing facts from perceptions and taking actionable strides can prove beneficial.

articles.title: Storm before Israel polls: Katz reacts to 'Netanyahu-IDF rift' over Iran strike plans
articles.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz has firmly denied rumors of discord between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and IDF Chief Eyal Zamir, despite rising concerns about possible military actions against Iran amidst an election cycle. Katz reassured that there are no current plans to strike Iran during this sensitive political time.

articles.title: 7-year-old Tripura boy writes alphabets of 30 languages, sets India Book record
articles.summary: Seven-year-old Rudransh Bhowmik achieved a remarkable feat by writing the alphabets in 30 different languages. He completed this impressive task in just 1 hour and 33 minutes using a pencil and paper. The languages included diverse scripts such as Arabic, Bengali, and Georgian, which present unique challenges. This record has been acknowledged by the India Book of Records, which promotes extraordinary achievements.

articles.title: Maine court upheld man's right to beach access despite neighbour's lawsuit
Five economic challenges ahead for new Brazil President Lula da Silva
articles.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will start his fourth term facing significant economic challenges. Rising public debt and high interest rates are squeezing government spending and increasing household financial strain. Lula’s reassurances about fiscal discipline conflict with pledges to raise the minimum wage faster than inflation. A conservative Congress may hinder his economic reform agenda, complicating essential fiscal measures.

articles.title: Florida court overturns home foreclosure after trial notice arrives too late
articles.summary: Robert Dwayne Harris has successfully appealed a foreclosure ruling against Nationstar Mortgage, LLC in Florida. The appeals court found that he did not receive adequate notice for his trial, which barred his defense from being presented. Acknowledging this oversight, Nationstar will now face a retrial in the lower court. Although the foreclosure sale proceeded, the court upheld the refusal of an injunction.

articles.title: How India plans to rebuild T-72, T-90 tanks using Soviet-era blueprints
articles.summary: Vehicle Factory Jabalpur is working alongside Heavy Vehicles Factory to overhaul Army tanks. The factory aims to develop indigenous designs for fixtures used in the tank overhaul process. Approximately 80 tanks are expected to be overhauled annually starting in April 2028. Training is ongoing for around 650 personnel as part of this project. The total estimated cost for the project is Rs 462 crore.

articles.title: Hulk Hogan's $3.3m Florida mansion sold by estate for $5.9m in 2026
articles.summary: Hulk Hogan's stunning mansion on Clearwater Beach has officially been sold for $5.9 million, following a series of price drops since its January 2026 listing. Originally priced at nearly $11 million, the sale marks a significant turn in the market for Hogan, who acquired the property in 2012 for around $3.33 million. Nearby, a quaint cottage also changed hands for $2.

articles.title: Minnesota court reverses reopening of 300-acre farm estate over 1989 will
articles.summary: In a significant Minnesota inheritance case, the state Court of Appeals has reinstated a 2017 ruling concerning the estate of farmer Clarence Vatthauer. Disputes arose from conflicting wills dated 1982 and 1989, leading to a previous court's decision being vacated. The appeals court's ruling underscored the necessity of procedural compliance and the need for finality in estate administration, reshaping the understanding of inheritance law.

October records highest number of ship attacks in Strait of Hormuz

This alarming spike highlights the escalating tensions amidst the ongoing US-Iran conflict. The International Maritime Organization has noted a total of 120 incidents in the broader region since the onset of hostilities, raising concerns for shipping companies and potential repercussions on global energy markets.

articles.title: Samsung told to refund Rs 98,000 with 9% interest over Z Flip6 screen failure

The company was ordered to reimburse Kapoor Rs 88,000 following identified service gaps tied to warranty shortcomings. Just after purchase, the phone showcased severe issues, which Samsung disputed by placing blame on alleged physical damages, but the commission found their evidence lacking.

As winter approaches, demand for refined products, especially diesel, is expected to rise significantly. Meanwhile, European countries face challenges due to reduced Russian gas imports exacerbated by the Iran war.

articles.title: Woman, lover kill father for opposing relationship; hide body in box
articles.summary: Pooja and her lover have been arrested for the murder of her father, Shyam Sundar Katheriya. The police discovered his decomposed body hidden in a box after neighbors reported a foul odor. Katheriya reportedly opposed Pooja's relationship, leading to suspicions about her involvement. His daughter, Kajal, expressed concerns over Pooja's behavior prior to the incident. A post-mortem examination will determine the cause of death while investigations continue.

articles.title: How damaged curd packet on Blinkit led to Rs 98,000 fraud in Bengaluru
articles.summary: A homemaker from Vasanth Nagar ordered curd online and received it in a damaged condition. After contacting customer service, she was guided by a fraudster through WhatsApp for a refund process. Following their instructions to upload a photo of the damaged packet led to another call from a different fraudster. Upon checking her digital payment account, she inadvertently entered her password, resulting in a significant financial loss.

articles.title: Crocodile meat bite in Thailand lands Ujjain official in hot water

The clip, reportedly shared by his wife, sparked controversy regarding his foreign travel. Rathore traveled to Thailand without obtaining the necessary permission for his trip. The Ujjain Municipal Corporation is now reviewing the situation for any potential rule violations.

articles.title: Gukesh vs Sindarov: What do world's top GMs think about the match?

From psychological pressure and opening preparation to experience and momentum, the 14-game duel promises a real battle of minds.

articles.title: Rs 1L penalty on Shangri-La for service charge

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi acquitted in 2018 defamation case by Sultanpur MP-MLA court
articles.summary:
Congress leader and Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi has been acquitted by an MP-MLA court in Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh, in a defamation case linked to remarks made during the 2018 Karnataka Assembly election campaign.

The case, filed by a BJP leader in 2018 over comments allegedly referring to Amit Shah as a “murder accused”, was dismissed by the court after nearly eight years of legal proceedings.

articles.title: Why Poland wants a stronger relationship with India | The Hindu Editorial
articles.summary:
Why is Poland seeking a closer partnership with India?

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s visit to India highlighted growing cooperation in trade, technology, defence, critical minerals, renewable energy and geopolitical coordination. With India and the European Union preparing to finalise a landmark Free Trade Agreement, Poland is positioning itself as a key European partner for New Delhi.

This editorial explores what both countries stand to gain, the challenges that remain, and why the India-Poland relationship could become increasingly important in Europe’s engagement with India.

articles.title: Tensions flare in Hyderabad after eggs 'thrown' at idol during procession
articles.summary: Hindu organisations protested following an incident where eggs were allegedly thrown at a Durga Mata idol. The incident occurred during an immersion procession within Madanapet police station limits in Hyderabad. Police responded promptly after receiving a call and took the suspects into custody for investigation. A similar incident involving stone-pelting was reported during a Durga Visarjan procession in Maharashtra.

articles.title: Protests engulf Europe: People take to streets in France, Albania, Italy, Spain, Portugal
articles.summary: Thousands of people protested across Europe over the weekend, demanding action against rising living costs and government corruption. Demonstrations were reported in France, Italy, Albania, Spain, and Portugal, with varying degrees of violence. Clashes between protesters and police resulted in numerous arrests and injuries in several countries. Many demonstrators called for affordable housing, better education, and protection of public pensions.

articles.title: ‘200 seats haq hai hamara’: Congress puts its UP poll ambitions on Lucknow walls

State Congress leaders are using a grading model to evaluate constituencies based on organisational growth.

articles.title: Foreign investors withdraw Rs 48,056 crore in October as market selling continues
articles.summary: Foreign Portfolio Investors have withdrawn Rs 48,056 crore from Indian equities during October due to high crude oil prices. Selling eased slightly in a recent week, with some FPIs becoming net buyers for two days. Elevated oil prices and inflation concerns are contributing to deteriorating corporate earnings outlooks affecting investor confidence. Domestic institutional investors have somewhat mitigated the selling pressure on markets in recent weeks.

articles.title: 'When will you score runs?' Babar Azam's weaknesses exposed by ex-Pakistan player
articles.summary: Babar Azam's recent performances in the ODI tri-series have raised concerns regarding his ability to convert starts into significant scores. He scored 45 against Sri Lanka and 34 against England, failing to build on important beginnings. Former cricketer Tanveer Ahmed has highlighted weaknesses in Babar's batting against spinners, incoming fast deliveries, and short balls. He emphasized the need for Babar to address these vulnerabilities to improve his performance.

articles.title: ‘Give priority to local artisans’: PM Modi’s festive shopping appeal as Diwali approaches
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged citizens to support local artisans by prioritizing their products while shopping for festivals. He emphasized that doing so would strengthen the 'Vocal for Local' campaign and promote a self-reliant India. Modi highlighted successful local exports such as makhana and arhar dal to various international markets. Additionally, he discussed efforts aimed at reviving traditional skills and farming practices, including natural cotton cultivation.

articles.title: Kentucky court orders fresh review of $703,000 farm dispute after divorce
articles.summary: Mary and Fred Holden's property settlement agreed to equal ownership of their Kentucky farm. Disagreements arose regarding when the farm should be listed for sale after two years. After their son moved out, Mary requested the farm be sold or purchased by Fred. The appeals court found the agreement's wording ambiguous, requiring a fresh evaluation in family court.

articles.title: Ashton Kutcher and Mila Kunis expand $10M beach house after mudslides
articles.summary: Ashton Kutcher and Mila Kunis are planning a significant renovation of their Carpinteria beachfront property. The proposed changes include expanding the main residence and adding a swimming pool. They acquired the property in 2017 for $10.1 million and have seen its estimated value rise to about $17 million. The couple's plans involve the removal of a guest cottage to enhance the outdoor living space.

articles.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang says US rules pushed China toward self-reliance
articles.summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang pointed out that US export controls have significantly fueled China's semiconductor advancements. He remarked that these restrictions have compelled China to bolster its own chip production strengths. Huang also expressed strong faith in the US technology sector's resilience, despite heightened competition from China, and dismissed worries about an impending memory chip surplus, predicting ongoing demand for High Bandwidth Memory in the years ahead.

articles.title: IIT Madras graduates' hostel idea grows into over 1,500 foldable buildings
articles.summary: Modulus Housing, founded by IIT Madras graduates, focuses on manufacturing foldable buildings for quick assembly and transportation. Since 2018, it has provided over 1,500 modular structures across India and parts of Africa. The startup aims to improve access to essential infrastructure like schools and clinics, especially in rural areas. Recently, it raised ₹70 crore in funding to support further expansion and innovation.

articles.title: From unfinished books to 10-second reels: Is reading becoming lost art?
articles.summary: The growing preference for short-form digital content is raising concerns about children’s ability to engage with books and sustain attention. Educationists and experts examine declining reading habits, the role of examination-driven learning, and the impact of digital distractions. Drawing on research and Kerala’s library movement, the story explores ways to rebuild deep reading through schools, families and communities.

articles.title: Drone attack: Iran targets Kurdish opposition bases in Iraq
articles.summary: Iran's armed forces conducted a drone attack on the Komala group in Iraq's Kurdistan region. This operation reportedly caused significant damage and casualties to the group's infrastructure. Previous strikes on the Komala group have occurred since the regional conflict began in February. Iran accuses these opposition groups of receiving support from Israel, its longstanding adversary. The Kurdish opposition has denied allegations of receiving arms from Israel despite Iran's claims.

articles.title: Five IPOs to hit Dalal Street next week, targeting nearly Rs 2,600 cr from investors

These firms—EAAA India Alternatives, SFC Environmental Technologies, M K Sons Fine Jewels, BLS Polymers, and Bombay Coated and Special Steels—will utilize the capital for business expansion, working capital augmentation, and settling debts. articles.title: Centre rushes 250 RAF personnel to Arunachal after protests over hydropower project

A mob torched an NHPC office and a police station in Pasighat, injuring over 40 police personnel. The project, seen as a strategic counter to China’s mega dam, faces opposition from indigenous tribes fearing displacement and submergence of villages.

articles.title: Man spits gutkha from 3rd-floor balcony, dies after coming in contact with 11kV wire

Residents reported that his spit, while chewing gutkha, made contact with the 11kV line. Locals expressed anger towards the electricity company for neglecting their complaints about unsafe wiring. His landlord mentioned that officials had assured residents about addressing these high-tension line concerns.

articles.title: ‘Failed to pay rent’: How landlord’s complaint led to 1,600 fake Rs 500 notes

Preliminary findings suggest that this operation may be connected to an extensive counterfeit currency syndicate.
